processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h before hot rolling; shared pre-treatment for all conditions of this alloy.
Hot rolled at temperatures of 1050–950 °C to produce a 6 mm sheet; shared pre-treatment.
After hot rolling, air cooled to room temperature; shared pre-treatment.

processing_steps.method: single-stage heat treatment at 1050 °C for 3 min followed by quenching
processing_steps.cooling_medium: quenching to room temperature (water quench per Fig. 1 blue quench tank)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Defining step of the S1050 sample: '(2) heat treatment at 1050 °C for 3 min followed by quenching to room temperature, hereinafter referred to as S1050'.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix with annealing twins (Σ3-dominated) and equiaxed grains; nanoscale κ-carbide co-gridded with the austenite matrix; intragranular B2 particles; the elongated intergranular Cr7C3 precipitates seen in S1000 are absent because Cr7C3 dissolves at 1050 °C.
structures.number_of_phases: 3 (austenite, κ-carbide, B2; Cr7C3 only in S1000)

microstructure_list.region: bulk / grain interior and grain boundaries

phases_present.grain_size: 3.84 μm (effective grain size d_eff, twins included)
phases_present.texture: annealing twins with Σ3-orientation relationship to parent grains; dominant misorientation peak near 60°

phases_present.morphology: nanoscale particles co-gridded with austenite; faint superlattice reflections in SAED; orientation relationship [011]γ // [011]κ
dark faceted intra-granular particles in the austenite

defects.type: pores/microvoids (dark rounded pores observed in SEM)

grain_structure.texture: misorientation angle distribution dominated by a peak near 60° (Σ3 annealing twins)

precipitates.distribution: absent — intergranular Cr7C3 dissolves when temperature increases to 1050 °C

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack propagation vs. grain boundaries and twins
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After intergranular precipitates are eliminated in S1050, grains grow and special boundaries interfere with RHAGBs; further intergranular crack propagation is inhibited and cracks propagate along special boundaries (straight cracking) or are deflected, producing a hybrid intergranular + transgranular ductile fracture. Crack propagation energy rises to 26.64 J (from 9.87 J in S1000).
Cracks are seen to travel 'across the twins' (yellow dashed lines in Fig. 8c,d) and to be deflected at boundaries.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Slip bands on the quasi-cleavage plane are observed on the S1050 impact fracture surface (post-deformation fracture feature).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Cr7C3 at the austenite grain boundaries dissolves as the temperature is raised to 1050 °C; austenite grains grow relative to S1000 (3.17 μm → 3.84 μm); κ-carbide and B2 remain.
interfaces.interface_notes: Proportion of 'special' boundaries (Σ ≤ 29, by length) is 68.3 % for S1050 — the lowest of the three conditions (S1000 71.7 %, MHT 71.2 %).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Tensile: gauge length 25 mm, gauge width 4 mm, gauge thickness 5 mm, machined along the rolling direction. Impact: standard Charpy V-notch 5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm.
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Measured tensile and impact properties are the averages of three tests per condition

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve for S1050 (blue curve) in Fig. 4(a); corresponding true stress–true strain and strain-work-hardening curves in Fig. 4(b).

strain_hardening_rate.value: maximum ~2000 MPa at a strain interval of 0.20–0.22

service_conditions.stress_state: uniaxial tensile and dynamic Charpy V-notch impact loading

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: 42.8 J for S1050 vs 29.2 J for S1000 (S1050 higher)
26.64 J for S1050 vs 9.87 J for S1000
MHT impact toughness (55.1 J) is 29 % higher than S1050

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM specimens mechanically polished then etched in 40 ml HNO3 + 100 ml ethyl alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize matrix microstructure, annealing twins and grain-boundary precipitates; examine tensile and impact fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1050 shows an austenitic matrix with twins and no elongated grain-boundary precipitates (unlike S1000); tensile fracture is dimpled; impact fracture shows quasi-cleavage planes with slip bands and microcracks.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD probe on Zeiss Ultra 55 SEM; specimens chemically polished with colloidal silica without etching
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Grain boundaries with Σ ≤ 29 classified as low-energy (special) boundaries; Σ3 fraction limited to 2/3 maximum
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure effective grain size (including twins), misorientation angle distribution and proportion of special boundaries
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1050 effective grain size 3.84 μm; dominant misorientation peak near 60° (Σ3 twins); proportion of special boundaries (Σ ≤ 29) = 68.3 %.

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 TEM; specimens 0.5 mm thick ground to 80 μm and twin-jet electrochemically polished in 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % methanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase composition and precipitate sizes (κ-carbide, B2, Cr7C3)
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbide (3–10 nm) co-gridded with austenite ([011]γ // [011]κ); B2 particles 20–160 nm present intra-granularly; grain-boundary Cr7C3 dissolved at 1050 °C.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: C content not measurable by EDS; C calculated via lattice parameter equations (1) and (2)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Mn, Al, Ni and Cr contents of the austenite

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; constant strain rate 3 mm/min; specimen gauge length 25 mm, width 4 mm, thickness 5 mm; yield strength measured at 0.2 % offset
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1050: YS 945 ± 14 MPa, UTS 1113 ± 3 MPa, total elongation 55.8 ± 0.4 %; avg of three tests.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Ambient temperature; standard Charpy V-notch specimens 5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm; load–displacement curves recorded; energies separated into crack initiation and crack propagation energies
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure impact energy and separate crack initiation/propagation contributions
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1050 impact energy 42.8 ± 0.4 J (avg of three tests); crack propagation energy 26.64 J; displacement 6.30 mm.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated precipitation/precipitate strengthening σ_PPT = 216 MPa for S1050 (obtained as σ_YS − σ0 − σ_GR) is used to explain the maintained high yield strength; solid-solution and grain-boundary contributions are 609 MPa and 120 MPa respectively.

analytical_models.model_note: Applied to S1050 to decompose the yield strength.

analytical_models.equation_role: σ0 = 97 + 279 wt% C + 1.5 wt% Mn + 20.5 wt% Al + 2.9 wt% Ni + 3.9 wt% Cr
analytical_models.model_note: Gives solid-solution strengthening of 609 MPa for S1050.
Used to calculate the C content in austenite because EDS is unreliable for C; applied to the S1050 austenite composition.

unmapped_findings: Charpy V-notch impact energy of S1050 (single-stage heat treatment at 1050 °C for 3 min + water quench) = 42.8 ± 0.4 J, average of three tests; this value is reported in Table 1 and Fig. 5 but has no dedicated schema field.
Crack propagation energy of S1050 = 26.64 J (intermediate between S1000 = 9.87 J and MHT = 36.78 J); Charpy load–displacement displacement of S1050 = 6.30 mm.
Proportion of 'special' grain boundaries (Σ ≤ 29, by length) for S1050 = 68.3 % — the lowest among S1000 (71.7 %), S1050 (68.3 %) and MHT (71.2 %).

Austenite chemical composition of S1050 measured by EDS (Table 2): Mn 21.09 ± 0.86, Al 9.00 ± 0.11, Ni 2.19 ± 0.16, Cr 3.16 ± 0.17, C 1.22 ± 0.03 (Fe balance); C calculated via lattice-parameter equations.
Strengthening contribution decomposition for S1050: solid-solution strengthening 609 MPa, grain-boundary (Hall–Petch) strengthening 120 MPa, and derived precipitation strengthening σ_PPT = 216 MPa.
Solid-solution strengthening effects of S1000, S1050 and MHT are 601, 609, and 599 MPa respectively (values are similar).
Grain-boundary strength values of S1000, S1050, and MHT are 145, 120, and 63 MPa respectively.
Steel density measured by the drainage method is 6.78 g/cm^3, about 14 % lower than pure iron (7.87 g/cm^3).

The strain-hardening rate of all steels passes through three stages; in the second stage the strain-hardening rate reaches a maximum of 2000 MPa at a strain interval of 0.20–0.22 (statement applies to S1000, S1050 and MHT collectively).

Impact fracture of S1050 shows quasi-cleavage planes with slip bands and microcracks/microvoids, i.e., an intermediate fracture mode between the intergranular fracture of S1000 and the fully ductile dimpled fracture of MHT.
